camp.about: The camp gives excavation crews a place to sort supplies, mend tools and cook between shifts.

well.about: The stone lining keeps loose earth out of the spring. A low rim makes it easy to fill buckets.

quay_steps.about: Porters use the lowest dry step to board a boat. As the tide rises they move their baskets up the stone stair, one landing at a time.

workshop.about: The sawbench turns logs into beams and planks for houses and boats.

market.about: Island growers bring fruit and grain to market. The stalls pack provisions in clay jars for the road.

gateway.about: Fishing boats unload at the harbour plaza. The catch goes straight from the quay to the market stalls.

lodge.about: The lodge gives visiting crews a dry berth and a place to prepare for their next departure.

archive.about: The archive keeps harbour plans and trade records dry. Carved rings serve as seals for official documents.

observatory.about: Sight lines through the stone pillars help navigators mark the positions of stars throughout the year.

fountain.about: Water from the spring flows through the fountain into a basin faced with green stone.

temple.about: The temple courtyard hosts public ceremonies and feast days under the island's sun emblem.

log_cabin.about: Trappers shelter here between trips. The cabin gives them a dry bench for repairing traps and gear.

apothecary.about: The herbalist dries leaves on reed trays and keeps the roots in separate clay pots. A sprig tied to each lid tells an apprentice which plant grew it.

mess_hall.about: Crews bring their own bowls to the long tables. One cook can feed a whole shift while the hearth is hot and have the grain soaking for the next.

stilt_house.about: Timber posts carry the sleeping floor above the flood line. A family can tie its boat to the steps and come home even when the lane is under water.

map_room.about: Cartographers combine soundings from different crews to mark reefs and channels on a single chart.

greenhouse.about: Tender seedlings spend their first weeks under cover. The gardener opens the shelter early, before the midday heat can wilt a whole bed.

trading_post.about: Quarry stone is squared and sorted here before it is traded to the island's builders.

water_mill.about: The stream turns the millwheel. Inside, millstones grind the island's harvest into flour.

clock_tower.about: The harbour watch tracks the tide from this tower. Pilots use its signals to time a shallow crossing.

lighthouse.about: A brazier above the harbour marks the entrance at night, when the reefs are hardest to see.

treehouse.about: Fruit pickers keep a sleeping platform among the branches. A watcher with a rattle can turn a flock away before it strips the ripest tree.

aviary.about: Crews carry homing birds aboard to send messages back to shore. The loft keeps the birds safe between voyages.

beached_ship.about: Shipwrights salvage valuable cargo and sound timber from the hull while the tide is out.

amphitheater.about: The amphitheatre gives the town a place for contests and public gatherings. Armourers set up their stalls at the entrance.

museum.about: The museum keeps the island's carvings and instruments together, where visitors can see how they were made.

hanging_gardens.about: Each terrace drains into the bed below. Gardeners carry water to the top at dawn and plant the thirstiest herbs where the first runnel falls.
